list/list: A vector is a list of numbers, kept in order. This one, x, holds four: three, minus one, four, and two.
list/dim: How many numbers it holds is its length, or its dimension. This x is four-dimensional, written x in R four. R stands for the real numbers, R four for every list of four of them, and in reads “is in”.
list/index: Each entry has an index: its position, written in square brackets. Python counts from zero, so x of zero is the first entry, three.
list/last: That makes the last of four entries x of three. There is no x of four.
image/image: Anything described by numbers can be a vector. Take a tiny color image, four pixels by four.
image/rgb: Each pixel is three numbers: how much red, how much green, and how much blue.
image/flat: Lay every number out in one row, and the image becomes a vector of four times four times three: forty eight entries.
image/big: A thirty two by thirty two color photo works the same way: three thousand and seventy two numbers in one vector.
ops/add: Two vectors of the same length add entry by entry: first plus first, second plus second, third plus third.
ops/scale: Multiplying by a number scales every entry. Two times u, written two u, doubles each one.
ops/same: The lengths have to match. Give v a fourth entry, and u has nothing to add to it.
